effectSize.note: The value function is terminal-dominant and the payoff scale is {-1, 0, +1}. When every candidate reaches a natural terminal, a decision can only produce a handful of distinct dQ values, so the label is a win/lose flip rather than a graded preference.

sampleSize.note: Order-of-magnitude arithmetic for a paired test at 95% confidence, not a formal power calculation. It assumes the observed discordance fraction holds, which this run is far too small to establish.

rootCauses: Positions sampled from Heuristic-vs-Heuristic episodes are largely decided: most candidates lead to the same winner, so dQ collapses to 0 and the decision is dropped.
The value function is terminal-dominant with a {-1, 0, +1} payoff, so surviving labels carry no magnitude information - only a sign flip.
A bounded heuristic continuation is used on both sides, which further reduces the spread between candidates relative to a stronger reference.
Root-family holdout splits a small label set into even smaller train/holdout sets: 7 train vs 1 holdout decisions here, which cannot distinguish any two arms.

recommendations.action: Sample decisions from contested positions, not uniformly from an episode
recommendations.why: Yield, not budget, was the binding constraint: 32 of 40 compared decisions were dropped as uninformative. Filtering for positions where the game is still open raises yield directly.
recommendations.costNote: Requires a cheap pre-filter (e.g. material balance or heuristic score gap) before spending the expensive continuation budget.

recommendations.action: Give the value function magnitude, or use a stronger reference policy
recommendations.why: With a {-1, 0, +1} payoff every surviving label has the same effect size, so any ranker can at best learn a coin flip. A graded leaf value or a deeper reference teacher creates rankable differences.
recommendations.costNote: A deeper teacher multiplies per-decision cost; a graded leaf value is cheap but must be calibrated against natural terminals first.

recommendations.action: Collect labels from many more episodes before running the arm comparison again
recommendations.why: At the observed yield, a paired test at 5 percentage points needs on the order of 7685 compared decisions, and the per-decision cost was unknowns in this run.
recommendations.costNote: This is the dominant cost and should be authorised explicitly before it is spent.

recommendations.action: Do not read this round's arm comparison as evidence about the method
recommendations.why: One holdout decision cannot separate a trained ranker from an untrained one; the arms are expected to tie, and a tie here is an absence of data, not evidence of no effect.
recommendations.costNote: None - this is a reporting constraint.
